acks.detail: fleet/race.mjs:225-234 — sqliteStoreJson, the judge's live store reader — Every judge test injects `readStoreJson` (test_race.mjs:507-511), as the global constraint requires (no sqlite in the suite), so the real `sqlite3 <dbDir>/fleet.db 'SELECT store FROM tinybase LIMIT 1'` spawn never executes. Statically verified: query string and options are identical to status.mjs:79-80, and the path is right — orchestrator.mjs:161 opens `path.join(dbDir, safeName(pathId) + '.db')` with FLEET_PATH='fleet' (orchestrator.mjs:33), i.e. exactly `<dbDir>/fleet.db`. Only a real race's judge exercises it. [structural false-green: sandbox could not execute it against the target]

fleet/race.mjs:58-67,162-173 — gitExec and the clone/checkout/set-url sequence — All git subprocesses are injected (test_race.mjs:88-93), per the no-git-remote constraint. The suite asserts the recorded call sequence and replays it to assert the resulting origin config (test_race.mjs:239-263), which is the strongest check available without a live clone, but `git clone --no-hardlinks`, `checkout --detach <sha>` and `remote set-url origin <url>` are never actually run. One edge the static reading surfaces: if the launch checkout is itself on a detached HEAD whose commit is unreachable from any branch, the local clone would not carry it and the `checkout --detach` would fail — loudly, and before the manifest is written, so it is a clean refusal rather than a defect. [structural false-green: sandbox could not execute it against the target]

fleet/race.mjs:181-190 — a live race: K concurrent driveOne calls against detached-HEAD clones with re-pointed origins, through to the publish leg and a judge over real artifacts — Needs sandbox VMs, a GitHub remote and real OAuth/GH tokens; the suite stubs driveOne entirely. Static reading supports every leg — drive.mjs:393 defaults baseRef to 'HEAD' (fine detached), drive.mjs:492 resolves a relative planPath against each run's own repoDir, provision.mjs:224 pushes fleet-base to the per-VM ssh remote (not origin) so K siblings cannot collide on that ref, vmName is `fleet-<runId>` (provision.mjs:170) so VM names are distinct, and every drive.mjs write into the shared evidenceDir is runId- or vmName-qualified (gate-read-, stat-, pr-body-, sandbox-logs/<vmName>-<ts>/). RUNBOOK:250 precedents three concurrent drive-one processes, but never three that each also own a fresh clone with a rewritten origin. The first real race is the only confirmation, and it is also what populates the pre-registered dials (fleet/race.mjs:38-50). [structural false-green: sandbox could not execute it against the target]
